add.title: LGBT rights in Brazil
add.summary: Wikipedia's 'LGBT rights in Brazil' (fetched and read in full, 28 Sep 2026) documents, in its Politics section, that LGBTQ people have a special place in Brazilian prisons, separate from other prisoners; that transgender people have the right to be called by their social name and not their birth name and to be forwarded to women's prisons; and that LGBTQ prisoners may choose male or female clothing. Footnoted (ref. 253) to a Mix Brasil (UOL) piece archived 18 Jan 2012 - c.2012-era source; placement-follows-identity practice for Brazil, recency not re-verified.

add.title: LGBTQ people in prison
add.summary: Wikipedia overview (fetched and read in full, 28 Sep 2026): its Brazil section does not report any trans-prisoner housing rule for Brazil (nor for Rio Grande do Norte specifically) - only vulnerability/stigma effects on travesti and transgender rehabilitation. Negative evidence corroborating that no state-level RN placement policy is documented in this overview.
